title: A Complete Tool Window
summary: This lesson assembles the chapter into one application: **Delve Inspector**, a tool with a docked layout that connects to a running copy of Delve and shows its live stats, monsters, a memory view of the telemetry block and a command panel, with a command palette, settings that persist, and the hardening from chapter 12. It is the template for the tools in chapter 18's capstones.
markdown:
## The layout ``` ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ File View Game Help ● connected · delve 18324 │ ├───────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Overview │ Frame time ▁▁▂▁▁▇▁▁▂▁▁▁▁▂ avg 8.2 ms · worst 21.4 ms │ │ floor 3 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ turn 412 │ Monsters [ filter: gob ] │ │ hp 14 / 20 │ Id │ Kind │ Position │ HP │ │ monsters 6 │ 3 │ goblin │ 17, 9 │ 6 │ │ │ 7 │ goblin │ 20, 4 │ 9 │ │ [Heal] [God] ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ Telemetry block (hex) │ │ │ 0000 44 4C 56 54 01 00 00 00 40 00 00 00 ... DLVT....@ │ └───────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` With ImGui's **docking** (enable `ImGuiConfigFlags_DockingEnable`; the vcpkg port's `docking-experimental` feature on versions where docking lives on its own branch), each panel is an ordinary `Begin`/`End` window that the user can dock, undock, tab and rearrange, and the arrangement is saved with the layout (lesson 14.05). ## The structure ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Platform["Platform layer"] CN["Connection
find process, map telemetry, pipe (12.01, 12.05)"] end subgraph Model["Model (pure logic, unit-tested)"] SN["Snapshot + validation (12.04, 12.07)"] HI["Histories, statistics (12.05)"] TB["Table rows, filter, sort (14.04)"] ST["Settings (14.05)"] end subgraph Views["Views (ImGui panels)"] OV["Overview"] FT["Frame time"] MO["Monsters"] HX["Hex view (12.02)"] CM["Commands + palette"] end CN --> SN --> HI SN --> TB HI --> FT TB --> MO SN --> OV SN --> HX CM --> CN ``` Three layers, as chapter 12 recommended: a thin **platform** layer that talks to the game, a **model** of pure, tested logic, and **views** that only draw the model and send user actions back. Each view is a function a few dozen lines long. ## The frame ```cpp-norun void Inspector::frame() { m_connection.poll(); // reconnect if needed; read a snapshot at most every 100 ms if (auto snap{ m_connection.latest() }) m_model.update(*snap); ImGui::DockSpaceOverViewport(); drawMenuBar(); drawOverview(); // reads m_model only drawFrameTimes(); drawMonsters(); drawHexView(); drawCommandPalette(); // Ctrl+P if (m_showDemo) ImGui::ShowDemoWindow(&m_showDemo); } ``` Commands ("heal", "god", "goto 3") go to the game through its command pipe (lesson 12.01) as console lines (lesson 11.07), never by writing into the game's memory: the game stays in charge of its own state, and the tool works with any build that understands the commands. ## The command palette Tools grow many commands. A **command palette** (Ctrl+P, as in many editors) lists them all, filtered as you type by **fuzzy matching**: typing `gt3` finds "Goto floor 3". Matching characters in order, with bonuses for matches at the start of words, ranks useful results first. The practice task implements the scoring. ## Finishing touches - **Status bar**: connection state, game version, telemetry version (lesson 12.06), last error. - **Keyboard shortcuts** for common actions, shown in menus. - **Logging** of the tool's own actions and errors to a file (lesson 8.03). - **Hardening**: the six failure modes of lesson 12.07, rehearsed. - **Packaging**: like lesson 11.08, a Release build with its DLLs, licences (ImGui's MIT licence, SDL's zlib) and a readme. ## Common mistakes > [!warning] Views that compute > Keep logic in the model, where it can be tested; views only draw and forward actions. > [!warning] Tools that write into the game's memory > Send commands through the game's interface and let it change its own state. > [!warning] A tool with no status > Always show whether it is connected, to what, and whether the data is current. ## Knowledge check ```quiz ? What are the three layers of the inspector? + A platform layer that talks to the game, a model of pure logic, and ImGui views that draw the model - Input, update and render - Debug, Release and Shipping > Separating them keeps the logic testable and the views simple. ? How does the inspector change things in the game? + By sending commands through the game's command pipe, which the game executes itself - By writing into the game's memory - By editing the save file > The game stays in charge of its own state. ? What does fuzzy matching in a command palette do? + Finds commands whose names contain the typed characters in order, ranking better matches first - Matches only exact names - Sorts commands alphabetically > `gt3` finds "Goto floor 3". ```

cards.q: What does ImGui docking add to a tool?
cards.a: Users can dock, undock, tab and rearrange panels, and the arrangement is saved with the layout.

cards.q: Why should views only draw and forward actions?
cards.a: So all logic lives in the model, where it can be unit-tested, and views stay short and simple.

cards.q: What should a tool's status bar show?
cards.a: Whether it is connected and to which process and version, the telemetry format version, and the last error.
